Mail and Packages reads the shipping notifications that arrive in your mailbox
and tells Gladys which parcels are on their way, arriving today, waiting to be
picked up, delivered, or stuck. It understands 36 carriers and marketplaces
(UPS, FedEx, USPS, Amazon, DHL, DPD, GLS, Colissimo, Chronopost, Mondial Relay,
Hermes, Royal Mail, Correos, SEUR, InPost…) in English, French, German, Spanish,
Italian, Dutch and Polish. With USPS Informed Delivery, it also counts the
letters announced for the day.

It is inspired by the Home Assistant
[Mail and Packages](https://github.com/moralmunky/Home-Assistant-Mail-And-Packages)
integration.

## Privacy

- The mailbox is read over IMAP, **read-only**: nothing is moved, flagged,
  marked as read or deleted.
- Only the emails of the carriers you enable are downloaded; every other email
  is only seen by its sender and subject, and never stored.
- Nothing leaves your Gladys: no third-party service, no tracking API.
- The integration stores one small file (`/data/state.json`): the identifiers
  of the notifications already announced to your scenes, so a restart never
  fires them twice. No email content, no password.

## Configuration

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.
2. Fill in the **IMAP server**, the **port** and the **security** of your
   provider (see the table below), then your **user name** (usually your email
   address) and your **password**.
3. Pick the **folders** to scan: `INBOX` by default. Separate several folders
   with commas, e.g. `INBOX, Shopping`. Gmail labels are folders too.
4. Uncheck the **carriers** you never use, if you wish. Shops or local carriers
   missing from the list can be added in **Other senders**, as addresses
   (`orders@shop.example`) or domains (`shop.example`).
5. Save, then click **Test the connection**: the message under the button says
   how many emails of the period are readable.
6. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the devices you want.

### Server settings by provider

| Provider          | IMAP server           | Port | Security | Password                                                                      |
| ----------------- | --------------------- | ---- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gmail             | `imap.gmail.com`      | 993  | TLS      | [app password](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833)             |
| iCloud            | `imap.mail.me.com`    | 993  | TLS      | [app password](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102654)                        |
| Yahoo             | `imap.mail.yahoo.com` | 993  | TLS      | app password (Account security)                                               |
| Outlook / Hotmail | —                     | —    | —        | Microsoft no longer accepts passwords over IMAP: forward to another mailbox   |
| GMX               | `imap.gmx.net`        | 993  | TLS      | enable IMAP in the GMX settings                                               |
| Orange            | `imap.orange.fr`      | 993  | TLS      | your password                                                                 |
| Free              | `imap.free.fr`        | 993  | TLS      | your password                                                                 |
| Your own server   | its name or IP        | 993  | TLS      | turn on **Accept a self-signed certificate** for a home-made certificate only |

**Tip — a dedicated mailbox.** You do not have to give Gladys access to your
main mailbox: create a free mailbox for Gladys only, and add a forwarding rule
from your main mailbox for the emails of your carriers. The original sender is
kept by most forwarding rules ("redirect" in some webmails); if it is not, add
your own address to **Other senders**.

### Advanced settings

- **Scan interval**: the mailbox is read every 5 minutes by default.
- **Days of emails to read**: a parcel is followed as long as its emails are
  younger than this (10 days by default). Archiving or deleting the emails of
  a parcel removes it from the counters at the next scan.
- **Language of the device names**: the names Gladys gives the devices when
  they are created. You can rename them afterwards.
- **Time zone**: decides when "today" starts. Empty: the time zone of the
  Gladys server.

## Devices

- **Mail and Packages** — the summary of every carrier:
  - _In transit_: every parcel still on its way;
  - _Arriving today_: parcels announced "out for delivery" today;
  - _Delivered today_;
  - _To pick up_: parcels waiting in a locker, a pickup point or a post office;
  - _Delivery problems_: delays, missed attempts, returns;
  - _Mail expected today_: the letters announced by USPS Informed Delivery;
  - _Last update_: the latest parcel event, as text.
- **Packages – _carrier_** — the same five counters for one carrier.

The counters are rebuilt from the mailbox at every scan: a second scan never
counts the same parcel twice.

## Scenes

### Triggers

In the scene editor, category **Integrations**:

| Trigger                    | When                                         |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Package shipped            | a shipping confirmation arrives              |
| Package out for delivery   | a carrier announces a delivery for today     |
| Package ready for pickup   | a parcel waits in a locker or a pickup point |
| Package delivered          | a carrier confirms a delivery                |
| Delivery problem           | delay, missed attempt, return to sender      |
| Letter mail expected today | the USPS Informed Delivery digest arrives    |

Each parcel trigger can be filtered on one or several carriers, and exposes
to the following actions: `{{triggerEvent.data.carrier_name}}`,
`{{triggerEvent.data.tracking}}`, `{{triggerEvent.data.tracking_url}}`,
`{{triggerEvent.data.pickup_code}}` and `{{triggerEvent.data.subject}}`. Each
parcel step fires once, restarts included; the emails already in the mailbox
when the integration is installed do not fire.

Example: _Package ready for pickup_ → send the message "Your
\{\{triggerEvent.data.carrier_name\}\} parcel waits for you, code
\{\{triggerEvent.data.pickup_code\}\}".

### Actions

- **Scan the mailbox for packages** — reads the mailbox now, then returns the
  counters.
- **Get the package counters** — instant: the counters of the last scan.

Both can target one carrier and return `arriving_today`, `in_transit`,
`pickup`, `delivered`, `exception`, `mail`, `expected_today` (true when a
parcel arrives today or waits to be picked up) and `summary`, a sentence ready
to send ("Packages: 2 arriving today, 1 to pick up."). Example: every morning
at 8, _Get the package counters_, then "Continue only if" `expected_today` is
true, then send the `summary` to the family.

## Dashboard widgets

- **Packages today** — the counters as tiles, the mailbox status, the time of
  the last scan and a **Scan now** button.
- **Package tracking** — the parcels on their way and today's deliveries, with
  the tracking number, the pickup code and a link to the tracking page of the
  carrier.

Both can show every carrier or a single one (widget settings).

## Troubleshooting

- **"The mail server refused the user name or the password"**: Gmail, iCloud
  and Yahoo require an app password, and two-step verification must be on to
  create one.
- **"Folder … does not exist"**: folder names are case-sensitive; Gmail's
  "All Mail" folder is `[Gmail]/All Mail` (or its translation).
- **A parcel is not detected**: check that its carrier is checked, and that
  the email is in a scanned folder and younger than the period read. Carriers
  change their wording from time to time: open an issue on
  [GitHub](https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Mail-and-Packages/issues) with
  the sender address and the subject of the email (remove your personal data).
- **Logs**: in Gladys, open the integration's **Supervision** page. Set the
  `LOG_LEVEL` variable to `debug` for details; the password is never logged.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Mail and Packages asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your mailbox | `section` | No | The integration reads the shipping notifications of your mailbox over IMAP, read-only: nothing is moved, flagged or deleted. Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo and Outlook require an app password, not your usual password. A dedicated mailbox, to which you forward your shipping emails, works too. |
| IMAP server | `string` | Yes |  |
| Port | `number` | Yes | 993 with TLS, 143 with STARTTLS. |
| Security | `select` | Yes |  |
| User name | `string` | Yes |  |
| Password (or app password) | `secret` | Yes |  |
| Folders | `string` | Yes | Folders to scan, separated by commas (e.g. INBOX, Shopping). Gmail labels are folders. |
| Accept a self-signed certificate | `boolean` | No | Only for a mail server on your own network. Leave off for an online provider. |
| Carriers | `section` | No | One device per checked carrier shows up in the Discovery tab, next to the "Mail and Packages" summary device. |
| Carriers to detect | `multi_select` | No |  |
| Other senders | `string` | No | Shops or carriers missing from the list: addresses or domains, separated by commas. Counted under "Other senders". |
| Advanced | `section` | No |  |
| Scan interval (minutes) | `number` | No |  |
| Days of emails to read | `number` | No | A parcel stays "in transit" as long as its emails are younger than this. |
| Language of the device names | `select` | No |  |
| Time zone | `string` | No | Decides when "today" starts. Empty: the time zone of the Gladys server. |

## How to install Mail and Packages in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Mail and Packages appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/gboulvin/gladys-mail-and-packages:1.0.2`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Mail-and-Packages](https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Mail-and-Packages).

Mail and Packages requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Mail and Packages is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [gboulvin](https://github.com/gboulvin), not by the Gladys core team.
